I will not start from empty talk. I farm by what worked on my land last year and what I saw in nearby fields around Quzhou. I have only 5 mu, so every bag of fertilizer costs real money, but if I cut fertilizer too hard and lose yield, that hurts more than wasting a little. I have well water, so I will not be too stingy with irrigation, especially on wheat jointing stage and cotton flowering stage. With my years in the field, I do not chase fancy changes fast. For maize, I will still use hybrid seed because that is what gives steady ears here. For wheat and cotton, I will use the improved seed I can trust from the dealer or what neighbors used well last year. On my small area, I will keep the work simple: plough or rotary tillage where it is convenient, put enough base fertilizer in, then topdress when the crop is pulling hard. Cotton needs more watching for insects, so I will spray it more times. Wheat is steadier, maize is in the middle. I will split the 5 mu across the three crops so the house has grain and cash crop both, and I will manage each one a little carefully because some people in my family work off-farm and labor at peak time is tight.
